content: CHENNAI: Diagnosed with Eisenmenger’s syndrome (a heart defect that also affects lungs) from birth, Aparna Kamakshi found great pleasure in writing. A passion, which she shared along with her mother Padmini Viswanathan. Together, they researched, wrote and self-published books, but Aparna’s biggest dream was to start a community blog for people who wrote for the joy of writing. But her condition got worse and she died in January 2018. Now, her mother has taken it upon herself to realise Aparna’s dream and launched the website Penning For Pleasure as a tribute to her daughter. “My daughter and I wanted to start a community blog where people could share their articles, stories or poems. There are many who do not know where to share their work. This can serve as a platform for like-minded people,” says 69-year-old Padmini, who with Aparna, her younger daughter, ran a monthly comic for the Kalki group for a few months in 2016. “My daughter loved reading Georgette Heyer, biographies, and writings of Dalai Lama. She used to write stories for children,” says Padmini. Aparna was her constant companion in all her endeavours. “With her medical condition, she needed a heart-lung transplant, but we were initially hesitant as the success rate for lung transplant wasn’t high. But by the end of 2017, when her condition deteriorated, we opted for one,” says Padmini. Aparna had her transplant in January 2018. “She was improving and was supposed to be discharged in a few days but suddenly developed sepsis and passed away. She was 43,” says Padmini. In June 2018, she launched penningforpleasure.com, which has separate sections for poems, stories, articles, travel and humour. “About 30 people wrote in but I didn’t know how to create more awareness about the platform or increase reader base,” says Padmini, who then conducted a competition to attract more people. She also finished a book she had begun penning with Aparna, ‘Be The Book: The Self Publishing Route to Self Discovery’. “My elder daughter, architect and dancer Krithika Subramaniam, wanted me to write it as we had learned so much about life even as we went about getting our books published,” says Padmini, who is now on the lookout for people who can help her run the blog. “I am not tech-savvy and don’t know how to regulate feedback,” she says. “I want someone to help me redesign and expand it. For me, it’s a tribute to my daughter and I am desperate to keep it going.” Download The Times of India News App for Latest City News.
